scenario.title: Support backlog
scenario.initial_request: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

M-IBAN-FAILURE-COUNT.name: Count of refunds with FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT status

M-TICKET-MEDIAN-RESPONSE.name: Median ticket response time versus SLA

M-REFUND-TICKET-LINKAGE-RATE.name: Share of support tickets attributable to refund IBAN failures
M-REFUND-TICKET-LINKAGE-RATE.numerator: tickets tagged/categorized as refund-status or refund-failure related

F-01.statement: payment-db.refund_failures returned 5 refund records, all with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT.

F-02.statement: ticket-db.response_times reports a median response time of 2.0 hours against a 24-hour SLA across 900 tickets.

CL-01.statement: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

CL-02.statement: Customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly.

H-CHATBOT-FIXES-WAIT.statement: The support backlog exists because customers have no self-service channel for refund status, so a chatbot answering refund questions would eliminate the wait.

H-PAYMENT-PROCESSING-DELAY.statement: Tickets and wait times are driven by actual delays in refund payment processing (DA-PAY), not by a lack of a self-service answer channel; a chatbot would not shorten the real wait.

H-SUPPORT-PROCESS-THROUGHPUT.statement: Backlog is caused by support agent/process inefficiency within P-REF (e.g. steps or handoffs), making ticket response times slow regardless of customer self-service options.

H-AGENT-DATA-ACCESS-GAP.statement: Agents lack timely access or integration to refund payment status (DA-PAY) when handling tickets, so they cannot answer quickly even though the information exists.

H-IBAN-FORMAT-REFUND-FAILURE.statement: Refunds fail at submission due to invalid/malformed IBAN format, blocking completion until corrected, and this failure mode is the proximate driver of refund-related tickets.

interpretation_history.interpretation: All 5 refund records returned by payment-db.refund_failures (E-01) are in status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, showing a real, recurring refund-processing failure mode in DA-PAY rather than a mere lack of a self-service answer channel. This does not yet establish how many support tickets these failures generate; that link is still unverified.

ticket-db.response_times (E-02) shows a median ticket response of 2.0 hours against a 24-hour SLA across 900 tickets, i.e. tickets are on average answered far inside SLA. This undercuts the premise that customers are stuck waiting because of slow ticket handling, and says nothing yet about why refund tickets are generated in the first place.

E-03.content: Customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-SUP (the requester, with a known bias toward framing issues as response speed) restates the original request in interview, asserting customers wait and a chatbot would answer instantly; this is a non-authoritative opinion, not new evidence, and does not establish ticket volume, cause, or response-time data.

U-TICKET-CAUSE-LINK.question: What proportion of the 900 tickets are specifically about refund status/IBAN failures versus other topics?
U-TICKET-CAUSE-LINK.decision_impact: Determines whether fixing IBAN validation would meaningfully reduce support ticket volume or whether other ticket causes also need to be addressed.
U-TICKET-CAUSE-LINK.resolution_path: Query ticket-db for ticket category/subject tags and cross-reference against DA-PAY failed-refund records.
U-TICKET-CAUSE-LINK.safe_placeholder: Proceed with IBAN-validation remediation as a parallel improvement without claiming it alone resolves the backlog until linkage is confirmed.

U-IBAN-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE.question: Why do refunds fail with FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT: customer input error, missing entry-time validation, or an integration bug?
U-IBAN-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether the appropriate fix is customer-facing input guidance, backend validation logic, or an integration repair.
U-IBAN-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Inspect the refund submission flow and payment-db validation logic for the 5 failed records.
U-IBAN-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Flag failed refunds for manual review/correction without changing validation logic until the cause is confirmed.

U-BANK-API-ACCESS-ISSUE.question: Does the bank-api ACCESS_DENIED/HOLD condition (recovery_decision event, seq 47) affect refund settlement independently of the sampled IBAN-format failures?
U-BANK-API-ACCESS-ISSUE.decision_impact: If related, an IBAN-validation fix alone would not resolve refund completion; a separate access/integration fix would also be required.
U-BANK-API-ACCESS-ISSUE.resolution_path: Review bank-api access configuration and determine whether settlement_status calls relate to the sampled refund failures.
U-BANK-API-ACCESS-ISSUE.safe_placeholder: Treat the bank-api DEGRADED/HOLD condition as a separate incident track; do not block IBAN remediation planning on its resolution.

A-TICKET-GENERATION-LINK.statement: IBAN-format refund failures are assumed to generate a meaningful share of refund-related support tickets, though E-01's own interpretation notes this link is not yet established.

A-SAMPLE-RECENCY.statement: The 5 refund_failures records in E-01 are assumed to reflect the current/ongoing failure pattern rather than an already-resolved historical batch.

SC-FIX-TARGETS-ROOT-CAUSE.statement: The remediation must address the IBAN-format refund failures identified in payment-db rather than only adding a self-service/chat layer on top of the unresolved failure.
SC-FIX-TARGETS-ROOT-CAUSE.threshold: measurable decrease from the baseline of 5 FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records
SC-FIX-TARGETS-ROOT-CAUSE.validation_method: Re-run payment-db.refund_failures after the fix and confirm the failure count decreases from the committed baseline.

SC-MAINTAIN-SLA.statement: Ticket response time should remain within the existing 24h SLA while any changes are made.
SC-MAINTAIN-SLA.validation_method: Re-run ticket-db.response_times periodically and compare the median against the 24h SLA.

VOB-R-2.unresolved_question: What specific mechanism (customer input error, missing client-side validation, or integration bug) causes refunds to fail with FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, since the validation logic recommended depends on this cause (U-IBAN-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE OPEN)?

problem_definition.requested_solution: Build a customer-facing chatbot so customers get instant answers about refunds instead of waiting (SH-SUP, CL-01).
symptoms: All 5 sampled refund records in payment-db are in status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, meaning refunds are not completing at submission (E-01).

Support lead reports customers 'wait forever' for refund answers and requests a chatbot (CL-01, CL-02), but ticket-db shows a 2.0h median response time against a 24h SLA across 900 tickets (E-02), contradicting a response-speed explanation.
problem_definition.root_problem: Refund requests recorded in payment-db (DA-PAY) are failing at submission with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT — all 5 sampled refund_failures records show this status (E-01) — blocking refund completion until the IBAN is corrected. This payment-processing failure, not a lack of a self-service answer channel or slow ticket handling (ticket-db shows a 2.0h median response against a 24h SLA across 900 tickets, E-02), is the best-supported driver behind the refund-related support activity that prompted the chatbot request.

structural_remedies.description: Add/strengthen IBAN format validation at refund-submission entry point in P-REF so malformed IBANs are rejected or corrected before persisting as FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT in DA-PAY.
structural_remedies.rationale: Matches the already in-scope action recommend_iban_validation_fix:DA-PAY and directly targets SC-FIX-TARGETS-ROOT-CAUSE; recommending/specifying the fix is feasible within remaining 225 min as a design deliverable even though live deployment and re-measurement happen later.; residual gap: Why IBANs are entering malformed (customer typo vs missing client-side validation vs integration bug) is still unverified (U-IBAN-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE OPEN), so the specific validation logic to add is not yet fully determined.

structural_remedies.description: Have payment operations correct and resubmit the 5 identified FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT refunds in DA-PAY as an immediate operational action, independent of the systemic fix.
structural_remedies.rationale: payment-db is HEALTHY and the 5 affected records are already enumerated in E-01/F-01, so this is a bounded, low-complexity ownership action.; residual gap: Only clears the sampled 5 instances; does not prevent recurrence of the FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT pattern for future refunds until entry-time validation (ADD-IBAN-ENTRY-VALIDATION) is in place.

structural_remedies.description: Introduce a process/data change to categorize or tag support tickets as refund-status/IBAN-failure related in DA-TCK, to quantify M-REFUND-TICKET-LINKAGE-RATE and close VOB-U-TICKET-CAUSE-LINK.

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: Refund submissions fail validation with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT in payment-db (DA-PAY), observed in all 5 sampled refund_failures records (E-01). → This failure blocks refund completion until the IBAN is corrected, per the supported hypothesis H-IBAN-FORMAT-REFUND-FAILURE (E-01). → Customers affected by a blocked refund are presumed to open or follow up on support tickets about refund status (assumption; this link is not yet confirmed by evidence). → Ticket-db response-time data shows tickets are answered quickly (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets, E-02), ruling out slow agent response as the driver of any perceived backlog. → The requester (SH-SUP) frames the issue as customers lacking a self-service answer channel (CL-01, CL-02, E-03) and proposes a chatbot, but this framing is contradicted by E-01 and E-02 (H-CHATBOT-FIXES-WAIT rejected).; rejected framings: [('H-CHATBOT-FIXES-WAIT', 'Contradicted by E-01 (refunds fail due to an IBAN-format processing defect, not absence of self-service) and E-02 (tickets already answered within SLA at a 2.0h median), so lack of self-service answering is not the supported cause.'), ('H-AGENT-DATA-ACCESS-GAP', 'Contradicted by E-02, which shows agents already respond within SLA, undermining the claim that agents lack timely data access.'), ('H-SUPPORT-PROCESS-THROUGHPUT', "Contradicted by E-02's fast median response time, which rules out agent/process throughput inefficiency as the driver.")]
[CONDITIONAL] critical unknown U-TICKET-CAUSE-LINK deferred to VOB-U-TICKET-CAUSE-LINK

This payment-processing failure, not a lack of a self-service answer channel or slow ticket handling (ticket-db shows a 2.0h median response against a 24h SLA across 900 tickets, E-02), is the best-supported driver behind the refund-related support activity that prompted the chatbot request.

proposal.summary: The support lead (SH-SUP) asked for a customer-facing chatbot so customers "stop waiting" for refund answers (CL-01). Investigation found this framing was not supported: payment-db shows all 5 sampled refund records failing with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01, F-01), while ticket-db shows a 2.0h median response against a 24h SLA across 900 tickets (E-02, F-02) — i.e. tickets are answered fast, so slow response is not the real driver. The problem was therefore redefined (PD-1) as a refund-payment-processing failure (IBAN format rejection), not a self-service/communication gap; the chatbot hypothesis (H-CHATBOT-FIXES-WAIT) was rejected and the IBAN-failure and payment-delay hypotheses (H-IBAN-FORMAT-REFUND-FAILURE, H-PAYMENT-PROCESSING-DELAY) were supported. The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring the open question of how many of the 900 tickets are actually refund/IBAN related (U-TICKET-CAUSE-LINK) as VOB-U-TICKET-CAUSE-LINK. What was released is three deliverables within release_scope: a root-cause investigation of the IBAN failures (DA-PAY), a design/specification-level IBAN validation fix recommendation (DA-PAY), and an SLA-compliance monitoring deliverable (DA-TCK) — not the originally requested chatbot. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds, because the open verification obligations either fall outside the released scope (VOB-U-TICKET-CAUSE-LINK) or are not yet required at this stage (VOB-R-2, VOB-R-3), while bank-api remains DEGRADED and several design-time knowledge gaps are documented as known limitations rather than blockers.
key_points: Root problem as defined (PD-1): refunds in payment-db fail at submission with FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01, 5/5 sampled records), not a lack of self-service/chat channel.

Evidence E-02 (median 2.0h response vs 24h SLA, 900 tickets) contradicts the stakeholder's 'customers wait forever' framing (E-03/CL-02), which is flagged as a known bias of SH-SUP ('frames everything as response speed').
Hypothesis H-CHATBOT-FIXES-WAIT was REJECTED (contradicted by E-01, E-02); H-IBAN-FORMAT-REFUND-FAILURE and H-PAYMENT-PROCESSING-DELAY were SUPPORTED by E-01.
DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS (seq 79), deferring the critical unknown U-TICKET-CAUSE-LINK as VOB-U-TICKET-CAUSE-LINK rather than blocking the whole investigation.

Released scope (SD-1 release_scope) covers: investigate_iban_failure_root_cause:DA-PAY, recommend_iban_validation_fix:DA-PAY, monitor_ticket_sla_compliance:DA-TCK — the chatbot (requested_solution) itself was not built.

Release decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, no holds; VOB-U-TICKET-CAUSE-LINK's blocking scope (analyze_ticket_refund_linkage:DA-TCK) sits outside release scope, and VOB-R-2/VOB-R-3 are open but not yet required (non-critical / required BEFORE_PRODUCTION, not before this release).
The IBAN validation-fix work item is a design/specification deliverable only; it has not been deployed or re-measured in this session.
The bank-api tool is currently DEGRADED (runtime tool_health), relevant to the still-open VOB-R-3 question about ACCESS_DENIED/HOLD settlement effects.
limitations_explained: Open unknown U-IBAN-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE / VOB-R-2: the specific mechanism (customer input error, missing client-side validation, or integration bug) causing FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT is not established, so the recommended validation fix is based on an unconfirmed cause.
